paragraphs.text: translated by
1. Do homage unto Varuna's and Mitra's Eye: offer this solemn worship to the Mighty God,
paragraphs.original: नमो मित्रस्य वरुणस्य चक्षसे महो देवाय तदृतं सपर्यत ।
paragraphs.translit: namo mitrasya varuṇasya cakṣase maho devāya tadṛtaṃ saparyata |

paragraphs.text: Who seeth far away, the Ensign, born of Gods. Sing praises unto Surya, to the Son of Dyaus.
paragraphs.original: दूरेदृशे देवजाताय केतवे दिवस्पुत्राय सूर्याय शंसत
paragraphs.translit: dūredṛśe devajātāya ketave divasputrāya sūryāya śaṃsata

paragraphs.text: 2. May this my truthful speech guard me on every side wherever heaven and earth and days are spread abroad.
paragraphs.original: सा मा सत्योक्तिः परि पातु विश्वतो द्यावा च यत्र ततनन्नहानि च ।
paragraphs.translit: sā mā satyoktiḥ pari pātu viśvato dyāvā ca yatra tatanannahāni ca |

paragraphs.text: All else that is in motion finds a place of rest: the waters ever flow and ever mounts the Sun.
paragraphs.original: विश्वमन्यन्नि विशते यदेजति विश्वाहापो विश्वाहोदेति सूर्यः
paragraphs.translit: viśvamanyanni viśate yadejati viśvāhāpo viśvāhodeti sūryaḥ

paragraphs.text: 3. No godless man from time remotest draws thee down when thou art driving forth with winged dappled Steeds.
paragraphs.original: न ते अदेवः प्रदिवो नि वासते यदेतशेभिः पतरै रथर्यसि ।
paragraphs.translit: na te adevaḥ pradivo ni vāsate yadetaśebhiḥ patarai ratharyasi |

paragraphs.text: One lustre waits upon thee moving to the cast, and, Surya, thou arisest with a different light.
paragraphs.original: प्राचीनमन्यदनु वर्तते रज उदन्येन ज्योतिषा यासि सूर्य
paragraphs.translit: prācīnamanyadanu vartate raja udanyena jyotiṣā yāsi sūrya

paragraphs.text: 4. O Surya, with the light whereby thou scatterest gloom, and with thy ray impellest every moving thing,
paragraphs.original: येन सूर्य ज्योतिषा बाधसे तमो जगच्च विश्वमुदियर्षि भानुना ।
paragraphs.translit: yena sūrya jyotiṣā bādhase tamo jagacca viśvamudiyarṣi bhānunā |

paragraphs.text: Keep far from us all feeble, worthless sacrifice, and drive away disease and every evil dream.
paragraphs.original: तेनास्मद्विश्वामनिरामनाहुतिमपामीवामप दुष्वप्न्यं सुव
paragraphs.translit: tenāsmadviśvāmanirāmanāhutimapāmīvāmapa duṣvapnyaṃ suva

paragraphs.text: 5. Sent forth thou guardest well the Universe's law, and in thy wonted way arisest free from wrath.
paragraphs.original: विश्वस्य हि प्रेषितो रक्षसि व्रतमहेळयन्नुच्चरसि स्वधा अनु ।
paragraphs.translit: viśvasya hi preṣito rakṣasi vratamaheḷayannuccarasi svadhā anu |

paragraphs.text: When Surya, we address our prayers to thee to-day, may the Gods favour this our purpose and desire.
paragraphs.original: यदद्य त्वा सूर्योपब्रवामहै तं नो देवा अनु मंसीरत क्रतुम्
paragraphs.translit: yadadya tvā sūryopabravāmahai taṃ no devā anu maṃsīrata kratum

paragraphs.text: 6. This invocation, these our words may Heaven and Earth, and Indra and the Waters and the Maruts hear.
paragraphs.original: तं नो द्यावापृथिवी तन्न आप इन्द्रः शृण्वन्तु मरुतो हवं वचः ।
paragraphs.translit: taṃ no dyāvāpṛthivī tanna āpa indraḥ śṛṇvantu maruto havaṃ vacaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Ne'er may we suffer want in presence of the Sun, and, living happy lives, may we attain old age.
paragraphs.original: मा शूने भूम सूर्यस्य संदृशि भद्रं जीवन्तो जरणामशीमहि
paragraphs.translit: mā śūne bhūma sūryasya saṃdṛśi bhadraṃ jīvanto jaraṇāmaśīmahi

paragraphs.text: 7. Cheerful in spirit, evermore, and keen of sight, with store of children, free from sickness and from sin,
paragraphs.original: विश्वाहा त्वा सुमनसः सुचक्षसः प्रजावन्तो अनमीवा अनागसः ।
paragraphs.translit: viśvāhā tvā sumanasaḥ sucakṣasaḥ prajāvanto anamīvā anāgasaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Long-living, may we look, O Surya, upon thee uprising day by day, thou great as Mitra is!
paragraphs.original: उद्यन्तं त्वा मित्रमहो दिवेदिवे ज्योग्जीवाः प्रति पश्येम सूर्य
paragraphs.translit: udyantaṃ tvā mitramaho divedive jyogjīvāḥ prati paśyema sūrya

paragraphs.text: 8. Surya, may we live long and look upon thee still, thee, O Far-seeing One, bringing the glorious light,
paragraphs.original: महि ज्योतिर्बिभ्रतं त्वा विचक्षण भास्वन्तं चक्षुषेचक्षुषे मयः ।
paragraphs.translit: mahi jyotirbibhrataṃ tvā vicakṣaṇa bhāsvantaṃ cakṣuṣecakṣuṣe mayaḥ |

paragraphs.text: The radiant God, the spring of joy to every eye, as thou art mounting up o'er the high shining flood.
paragraphs.original: आरोहन्तं बृहतः पाजसस्परि वयं जीवाः प्रति पश्येम सूर्य
paragraphs.translit: ārohantaṃ bṛhataḥ pājasaspari vayaṃ jīvāḥ prati paśyema sūrya

paragraphs.text: 9. Thou by whose lustre all the world of life comes forth, and by thy beams again returns unto its rest,
paragraphs.original: यस्य ते विश्वा भुवनानि केतुना प्र चेरते नि च विशन्ते अक्तुभिः ।
paragraphs.translit: yasya te viśvā bhuvanāni ketunā pra cerate ni ca viśante aktubhiḥ |

paragraphs.text: O Surya with the golden hair, ascend for us day after day, still bringing purer innocence.
paragraphs.original: अनागास्त्वेन हरिकेश सूर्याह्नाह्ना नो वस्यसावस्यसोदिहि
paragraphs.translit: anāgāstvena harikeśa sūryāhnāhnā no vasyasāvasyasodihi

paragraphs.text: 10. Bless us with shine, bless us with perfect daylight, bless us with cold, with fervent heat and lustre.
paragraphs.original: शं नो भव चक्षसा शं नो अह्ना शं भानुना शं हिमा शं घृणेन ।
paragraphs.translit: śaṃ no bhava cakṣasā śaṃ no ahnā śaṃ bhānunā śaṃ himā śaṃ ghṛṇena |

paragraphs.text: Bestow on us, O Surya, varied riches, to bless us in our home and when we travel.
paragraphs.original: यथा शमध्वञ्छमसद्दुरोणे तत्सूर्य द्रविणं धेहि चित्रम्
paragraphs.translit: yathā śamadhvañchamasadduroṇe tatsūrya draviṇaṃ dhehi citram

paragraphs.text: 11. Gods, to our living creatures of both kinds vouchsafe protection, both to bipeds and to quadrupeds,
paragraphs.original: अस्माकं देवा उभयाय जन्मने शर्म यच्छत द्विपदे चतुष्पदे ।
paragraphs.translit: asmākaṃ devā ubhayāya janmane śarma yacchata dvipade catuṣpade |

paragraphs.text: That they may drink and eat invigorating food. So grant us health and strength and perfect innocence.
paragraphs.original: अदत्पिबदूर्जयमानमाशितं तदस्मे शं योररपो दधातन
paragraphs.translit: adatpibadūrjayamānamāśitaṃ tadasme śaṃ yorarapo dadhātana

paragraphs.text: 12. If by some grievous sin we have provoked the Gods, O Deities, with the tongue or thoughtlessness of heart,
paragraphs.original: यद्वो देवाश्चकृम जिह्वया गुरु मनसो वा प्रयुती देवहेळनम् ।
paragraphs.translit: yadvo devāścakṛma jihvayā guru manaso vā prayutī devaheḷanam |

paragraphs.text: That guilt, O Vasus, lay upon the Evil One, on him who ever leads us into deep distress.
paragraphs.original: अरावा यो नो अभि दुच्छुनायते तस्मिन्तदेनो वसवो नि धेतन
paragraphs.translit: arāvā yo no abhi ducchunāyate tasmintadeno vasavo ni dhetana
